between: museum-framework.md §4.5, display rules for Relationship Objects: "Alternatives are one interaction away from every bridge. Selecting a bridge shows its rivals at the same visual weight as itself, per §3.10's refusal to let layout settle a question."
and: museum-framework.md §12.3 constraint V-8: "Equal visual weight is a claim, and is only made where the evidence is equal. Two rival explanations rendered identically when their evidence differs fails §3.10." CLAUDE.md standing constraints, no false equivalence: "A contested claim and an established one do not get parallel presentation."
what_disagrees: Whether rival explanations are rendered at equal visual weight. §4.5 requires equal weight for a bridge's alternatives; V-8 forbids equal weight wherever the evidence is unequal. Both cite §3.10 as their authority.
measured: Not a measurement. Both passages read in full in 13-PRODUCT-ARCHITECTURE/museum-framework.md as committed on main: §4.5 display rules, and §12.3 constraint V-8.
severity: MEDIUM - it does not affect any evidentiary claim, but it governs how rival explanations are displayed, which is where false equivalence enters a product
resolvable_here: PARTLY. The two rules can be reconciled by scope, and experience-object-model.md §9.7 does so for the Challenge object: reachability is equal for every rival, weight follows evidence. Whether that reconciliation is what museum-framework.md §4.5 intended is the framework author's to say.
effect: experience-object-model.md §9.7 (Challenge rivals) is written against V-8 and CLAUDE.md rather than against §4.5 generalised, and says so at the point of use. An earlier draft of §9.7 asserted that the two rules were not in conflict and cited only §4.5; that was a preferred-counter-narrative failure and is logged as BF-022.
action: Referred to the museum framework for a scope note on §4.5 saying whether it is confined to a bridge and its alternatives. No register row is promoted or demoted by this. Queued in 04-AUDITS/REAUDIT-QUEUE.csv as RA-021.

between: museum-framework.md §4.4, the seven domains over which a relationship is a bridge and over which transitive closure is disabled: language, ancestry, culture, artifact, religion, polity, modern identity.
and: museum-framework.md §10.2 constraint 2, which requires that "Every environmental→culture link is a bridge with §4.4's required mechanism and rivals" - naming "environmental" as though it were one of the seven. 13-PRODUCT-ARCHITECTURE/water-living-world.md §3.2 inherits the same slippage, assigning slots the content domains environment, settlement, place, text and "the archive itself".
what_disagrees: Whether the vocabulary a slot's content is described in is the vocabulary bridges are typed in. It is not. "Environment" is not in the §4.4 enum, so an environment→culture bridge_type cannot be constructed, and M-6's transitive-closure rule - defined over domain boundaries - cannot be evaluated for slots 1, 4 or 6 at all.
measured: Yes, by enumeration. §4.4 lists seven domains; §10.2 constraint 2 and water-living-world.md §3.2 between them use at least five terms that are not among them.
severity: MEDIUM. It does not affect any evidentiary claim, and it does not weaken M-6 in the direction that matters - an unevaluable link is treated as unevaluable, not as permitted. It does mean the strongest anti-continuity rule in the framework has a gap in coverage precisely where an environmental thread runs.
resolvable_here: NO. The slippage originates in the framework, at §10.2 constraint 2, and extending §4.4's domain enum is the framework author's call. A specification that widened it on its own authority would be doing the thing this document spends §5 arguing against.
effect: water-living-world.md §9.1b records it and states the conservative reading: until it is resolved, any slot 1, 4 or 6 link is treated as unevaluable rather than as permitted. No claim is promoted or demoted.
action: Referred to the museum framework: either environment is an eighth domain, or §10.2 constraint 2 is restated in terms of the seven. Queued alongside RA-021 as a framework-level question this repository has now raised twice from a specification.

between: 13-PRODUCT-ARCHITECTURE/museum-framework.md section 1.7, the posture-to-mode matrix: Field Mode is forbidden in the Reading Room posture
and: museum-framework.md section 1.5 derivation rule 7, which makes Reading Room the residual for any exhibit the derivation cannot classify, flagged derived_residual = true; read with section 1.6.1
what_disagrees: Section 1.6.1 states that 'an exhibit does not become Reading Room by being unclassifiable' and that rule 7 makes Reading Room the residual ONLY for derivation, so the size of the unclassified set is visible 'rather than laundered into a posture count'. But section 1.7 attaches a hard prohibition to the posture VALUE, not to the posture FINDING. Composed, a derived_residual = true assignment silently forbids Field Mode on any exhibit the derivation cannot classify - a prohibition falling out of an admitted encoding defect rather than out of any judgement about the exhibit.
measured: Found while running the section 1.5 derivation for 06-BRIEFS/childrens-pilot/. That investigation's claim set does not fire rules 1-6 on a strict reading of rule 3 ('load-bearing propositions' resolving to 'typed absences'), so it falls to rule 7. Section 1.6.1 says that result is not a posture finding; section 1.7 would nevertheless forbid the mode.
effect: Any children's investigation whose derivation returns the residual is forbidden by default rather than assessed. The framework's own diagnosis of the residual as an encoding defect is what makes the default indefensible; section 1.7's rule is sound where Reading Room is an actual editorial assignment.
action: Framework revision, not this repository's registers. Candidate: scope section 1.7's Field prohibition to an ASSIGNED Reading Room posture with a written override reason, and state that derived_residual = true carries no mode consequence. Raised alongside D-055, which is the specific case. This contradiction does not excuse the children's pilot: if the owner ASSIGNS Reading Room, the specification is withdrawn whatever the tension.
